                                   7          The expedited discovery ordered by the presiding judge is limited to discovery needed to

                                  16   on an expedited basis. See generally Dkt. No. 110 at 4-7; Dkt. No. 110-1 (responses to RFPs 1-5).

                                  17          The Court addresses below each area of disagreement.

                                  18          A.      Apple Custodians
                                  19          As reflected in the joint submission, Apple has agreed to search the files of Dr. Shi, as well

                                  20   as the files of four Apple employees involved in Dr. Shi’s “offboarding” from the company:

                                  21   Mathieu Charbonneau-Lefort, Wesley Cheng, Martin Garfias, and Sandy Zhao. Dkt. No. 110 at 2,

                                  22   5. In addition, Apple is willing to search the custodial files of five custodians, to be selected by

                                  23   OPPO, from among the individuals identified in Apple’s trade secret disclosure (Dkt. No. 109-3)

                                  24   who had one-on-one meetings with Dr. Shi prior to his departure from Apple. Dkt. No. 110 at 5.

                                  25   The parties disagree about whether Apple should search the files of all individuals with whom Dr.

                                  26   Shi had one-on-one meetings or just the files of five such individuals selected by OPPO.

                                  27          The relevant document request is RFP 2, which asks for documents relating to the one-on-

                                  28   one meetings. Apple explains that of the 36 one-on-one meetings Dr. Shi had, only 19 included
                                                                                          2
                                            Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL         Document 120        Filed 10/29/25       Page 3 of 7




                                   1   discussions of Apple’s trade secrets. Dkt. No. 110 at 4-5. Given Apple’s present contention that

                                   2   trade secret information was shared with Dr. Shi during 19 one-on-one meetings before his

                                   3   departure from Apple, for RFP 2, Apple should produce responsive, non-privileged documents, if

                                   4   any, showing for each such meeting, the date of the meeting, the participants, and what was

                                   5   disclosed or discussed during the meeting. The Court expects that this will require a search of the

                                   6   relevant custodial files of all individuals identified in the trade secret disclosure for each of the 19

                                   7   meetings at issue, for the time period during which Dr. Shi had those meetings.3 Apple need not

                                   8   search the custodial files for any individual involved in the 17 other meetings that Apple now

                                   9   contends did not involve discussion of Apple’s trade secrets.

                                  10             The parties also disagree about whether other custodians’ files should be searched in

                                  11   connection with other RFPs. The Court addresses those disputes in the next section.

                                  12             B.     Search Methodology for Apple Custodial Files
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13             The parties disagree about whether, for RFPs 2-5, Apple should run “systematic searches,”

                                  14   using OPPO’s proposed search terms and date cutoffs for all custodial data for all relevant

                                  15   custodians, or whether Apple may use other means to identify responsive documents. See Dkt.

                                  16   No. 110 at 3, 5-6.

                                  17             As reflected in the joint submission, both OPPO and Apple have proposed search terms,

                                  18   although Apple’s proposal is limited to search terms to be applied only to Dr. Shi’s email. Dkt.

                                  19   No. 109-4 (OPPO); Dkt. No. 109-5 (Apple). OPPO argues that its 43 search terms are “targeted to

                                  20   the alleged trade secrets” and “mirror” the search terms Apple asked OPPO to apply to its own

                                  21   document collections, and thus should be applied to all custodial sources. Dkt. No. 110 at 3.

                                  22   Apple responds that it will apply OPPO’s search terms (other than Dr. Shi’s name) to Dr. Shi’s

                                  23   email and Slack custodial files from the period April 1-June 27, 2025, but will review Dr. Shi’s

                                  24   other custodial files using other, unspecified means. Id. at 6. In addition, Apple objects to

                                  25   applying OPPO’s search terms to all other custodial files, arguing that “the parties are not

                                  26   similarly situated” with respect to the need for expedited discovery. Id. Apple argues that for

                                  27

                                            Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL        Document 120         Filed 10/29/25     Page 4 of 7




                                   1   purposes of expedited discovery, it has interviewed employees with knowledge about the location

                                   2   of responsive documents and that this is the most efficient approach to identify such documents.

                                   3   Id.

                                   4            The Court agrees with Apple that for purposes of expedited discovery the parties’ needs

                                   5   are not the same, and thus, OPPO’s argument based on the similarity of its search terms and

                                   6   Apple’s is not particularly persuasive. In order to resolve the parties’ dispute, the Court considers

                                   7   the parties’ arguments about the appropriate search methodology in the context of the RFP at

                                   8   issue.

                                   9                   1.      RFP 1
                                  10            It is not clear whether there is any dispute about Apple’s obligation to produce “all

                                  11   documents” Apple has identified and that it contends contain Apple trade secrets. See Dkt. No.

                                  12   110-1 (RFP 1). OPPO says that Apple has only produced 54 of the hundreds of documents Apple
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   contends Dr. Shi took without permission. Dkt. No. 110 at 1. Apple’s position regarding RFP 1 is

                                  14   not clear, but in the Court’s view, there should be no need for Apple to limit its search for

                                  15   responsive documents to those it can locate “after a reasonable search of the location or locations

                                  16   where responsive documents are most likely to be located.” See Dkt. No. 110-1 (response to RFP

                                  17   1). Nor is there any need to apply search terms.

                                  18            If Apple contends that any of the documents within the scope of RFP 1 contain its trade

                                  19   secret information, Apple must produce all such documents. However, Apple need not produce

                                  20   documents within the scope of RFP 1 that it now contends do not contain its trade secret

                                  21   information. Apple must identify for OPPO all of the documents as to which Apple takes that

                                  22   position.4 If Apple contends that it cannot produce a trade secret document within the scope of

                                  23   RFP 1 because it no longer has the document, e.g., because the document has been removed from

                                  24   Apple’s possession, Apple must so advise OPPO.

                                  25

                                  26
                                  27   4
                                         Contrary to OPPO’s argument, there is no justification for expedited discovery of documents
                                  28   reflecting that Dr. Shi downloaded “innocuous material” that is not at issue or trade secret
                                       documents that Dr. Shi could have taken but did not. See Dkt. No. 110 at 3.
                                                                                        4

                                   1                   2.     RFP 2

                                   2           As noted above, RFP 2 asks for documents relating to the one-on-one meetings Dr. Shi had

                                   3   with Apple employees before he left the company. Because Apple must produce, for each of the

                                   4   relevant custodians for the relevant time period, all documents showing for each of the 19

                                   5   meetings, the date of the meeting, the participants, and what was disclosed or discussed during the

                                   6   meeting, the Court expects that the application of search terms to the custodial files of the

                                   7   individuals involved in the meetings will not be particularly useful in identifying documents

                                   8   responsive to RFP 2. While the custodians themselves must not conduct the document review on

                                   9   their own, Apple’s counsel may directly collect and review these custodial documents for the

                                  10   relevant time period, as Apple has proposed to do, without applying all of OPPO’s 43 search terms

                                  11   to the collection.

                                  12                   3.     RFP 3
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           RFP 3 asks for all documents “related to” Apple’s “invention, development,

                                  14   implementation, or commercialization” of all trade secrets Apple contends defendants

                                  15   misappropriated. See Dkt. No. 110-1 (RFP 3). Apple objects to the scope of RFP 3, and also to

                                  16   OPPO’s demand that it add custodians involved in development of the trade secrets and then apply

                                  17   OPPO’s search terms to those custodians’ files. Id. at 4, 5, 6. Apple represents it will produce

                                  18   responsive documents related to the “invention and development” of the trade secrets at issue that

                                  19   it can “locate after a reasonable search.” Id. (response to RFP 3).

                                  20           The Court is not persuaded that OPPO is entitled to any discovery relating to Apple’s

                                  21   development of the trade secrets at issue, beyond what Apple has already committed to provide at

                                  22   this time. If, as OPPO contends elsewhere, Apple’s alleged trade secrets are not unique to Apple,

                                  23   but are instead “ubiquitous in the category of wearable devices and beyond,” Dkt. No. 59 at 20,

                                  24   the Court questions why OPPO needs such comprehensive discovery from Apple regarding its

                                  25   development and implementation of these trade secrets in order to defend against Apple’s motion

                                  26   for a preliminary injunction. While such discovery may well be warranted at some point in the

                                  27   case, the Court agrees with Apple that the scope of discovery OPPO demands in RFP 3, and the

                                  28   search methodology it advocates, exceed the bounds of reasonable expedited discovery. See Dkt.
                                                                                         5
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL           Document 120         Filed 10/29/25      Page 6 of 7




                                   1   No. 48 at 14:7-8 (“We are not going to have all the case discovery happen in the next 30 days.”).

                                   2   The Court denies OPPO’s requested search methodology beyond what Apple has already agreed

                                   3   to search for and produce.

                                   4                  4.      RFP 4

                                   5          RFP 4 asks for all documents that “gave rise to, support, call into question, or otherwise

                                   6   relate to” Apple’s allegations of misappropriation. See Dkt. No. 110-1 (RFP 4). Apple responds

                                   7   that it has produced a forensic report of Dr. Shi’s Apple-owned devices and will produce other,

                                   8   unspecified responsive documents. Id. (response to RFP 4).

                                   9          While the Court agrees that Apple should produce documents tending to support or

                                  10   undermine its allegations of misappropriation, it is not clear why OPPO believes that Apple must

                                  11   apply search terms in order to identify responsive files, nor is it clear to which set of custodians’

                                  12   files OPPO believes the search terms should be applied. The Court expects Apple to review the
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   documents of the individuals involved in the investigation of Dr. Shi’s conduct, but OPPO does

                                  14   not offer a sufficient justification for requiring Apple to apply all of OPPO’s 43 search terms to

                                  15   these individuals’ files. The Court denies OPPO’s requested search methodology beyond what

                                  16   Apple has already agreed to search for and produce.

                                  17                  5.      RFP 5
                                  18          RFP 5 asks for all communications “with any third party, including but not limited to

                                  19   government authorities, relating to this action or Apple’s claims or allegations herein.” Dkt. No.

                                  20   110-1 (RFP 5). Apple represents that it will produce non-privileged, responsive documents that it

                                  21   can “locate after a reasonable search of the location or locations where responsive documents are

                                  22   most likely to be located.” Id. (response to RFP 5).

                                  23          OPPO does not explain why it requires this discovery in order to defend against Apple’s

                                  24   motion for a preliminary injunction. While such discovery may well be warranted at some point

                                  25   in the case, it is not within the scope of reasonable expedited discovery. The Court denies OPPO’s

                                  26   requested search methodology beyond what Apple has already agreed to search for and produce.

                                  27          C.      Apple Non-Custodial Sources
                                  28          The parties’ dispute regarding Apple’s search of non-custodial sources is not well-
                                                                                          6
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL          Document 120        Filed 10/29/25     Page 7 of 7




                                   1   developed in the joint submission. The Court has already rejected OPPO’s arguments that Apple

                                   2   should be required to search for and produce documents reflecting that Dr. Shi downloaded

                                   3   “innocuous material” that is not at issue or that Dr. Shi could have taken other documents but did

                                   4   not. See supra, note 4. In addition, OPPO argues that Apple has not been transparent about what

                                   5   non-custodial sources it is searching or how it is conducting those searches. Dkt. No. 110 at 4.

                                   6   Apple responds that it is searching two non-custodial sources: Apple’s Box.com repository, and

                                   7   an internal Apple University website. Apple asserts that its searches are “based on” Mr.

                                   8   Roffman’s declaration and “assistance from knowledgeable employees.” Id. at 6. The Court

                                   9   agrees that Apple’s description of its search methodology is vague. However, the parties have

                                  10   provided the Court insufficient information to assess whether any of these non-custodial sources is

                                  11   likely to have information OPPO actually needs for its defense to Apple’s preliminary injunction

                                  12   motion, and if so, what kind of information Apple needs to find and produce. In any event, to the
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   extent OPPO wishes Apple to search all repositories to which Dr. Shi had access, it is not clear

                                  14   how such a search will yield any information useful for OPPO’s defense.

                                  15          The Court denies OPPO’s request.

                                  16          D.      Deadlines for Apple’s Production
                                  17          Per the existing case schedule, OPPO’s opposition to Apple’s preliminary injunction

                                  18   motion is due November 19, 2025. Apple must substantially complete its production of

                                  19   documents, consistent with this order, by November 4, 2025. The Court expects the parties to

                                  20   work out a date for OPPO’s Rule 30(b)(6) deposition of Apple without the Court’s assistance.

                                  21          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  22   Dated: October 29, 2025
